extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — investigators, grant applicants, institutional administrators, and grant support staff
extracted.subtask_description: Index/news page summarizing recent NIH extramural funding policy updates, process changes, resources, and announcements intended to inform grant applicants and institutional staff about requirements and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select appropriate models for research (NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: "NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose models (including New Approach Methodologies) that are scientifically sound and justified by the research question; prioritize human relevance/translational potential only insofar as they are the best fit for the specific aims. No prescriptive single model — selection must be justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow PF5 Collaborative International Research Project application format
rubrics_metrics.description: "New Video Overview for NIH’s Collaborative International Research Projects (PF5) — Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use the PF5-specific application format and be aware that applications may be split into linked awards after peer review and prior to Just-in-Time (JIT) requests; review the PF5 overview resources for key features and formatting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: "2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing Plan Format Available — We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans for applicable submissions, use the 2026 Pilot format and include the simplified required elements specified in that format; consult the announced resource for exact required elements and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility in applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: "Embedding Replication and Reproducibility Throughout NIH Research: Key Reminders for Applications, Awards, and a New Highlighted Topic — The reliability of biomedical research is foundational... NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility. In support of this plan, NIH has launched a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications and awards should address replication and reproducibility considerations where appropriate; align proposals with NIH's emphasis on replicability (e.g., study design, statistical power, transparency) and consider whether the new Highlighted Topic or initiatives apply to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand 'Competitive But Not Discussed' review designation
rubrics_metrics.description: "My Application Was Scored as 'Competitive But Not Discussed' During Review. What Does This Mean? — Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should know that peer-review procedural changes can designate the middle third as 'competitive but not discussed,' meaning an application can receive favorable scores yet not be discussed; interpret summary statements and seek sponsor guidance on next steps (e.g., resubmission strategies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of centralized NIH peer review consolidation and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: "One Year Later: How Centralized NIH Peer Review is Strengthening Efficiency, Competition, and Transparency — In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR)... providing an update on the consolidation and its initial effects on the peer-review process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and institutions should understand that peer review processes and timelines may change due to centralization; be attentive to procedural updates from CSR that could affect study section assignment, review timing, and administrative processes.
